python3 -c "
import statistics

# First table (Net registered tonnage) - the correct table per the question
# Columns: Sept, Oct, Nov, Dec, Jan, Feb, Mar, Apr, May, June, July, Aug, Sept (1941)
# Note: page 91 shows 'Sept' twice - first Sept. 1940 (col 3), then Sept. 1941 (last col)
# First 1941 column is Jan (position 6 in 0-indexed from start of monthly data)

# American vessels - from first table (net registered)
american = [644, 608, 491, 486, 468, 489, 553, 680, 940, 1068, 1041, 930, 825]
# Grand total - from first table
grand_total = [3160, 3079, 2571, 1875, 1825, 1801, 2032, 2662, 3694, 4177, 4791, 4657, 3837]

print('American vessels series:', american)
print('Grand total series:', grand_total)
print('Length American:', len(american))
print('Length Grand:', len(grand_total))

# Compute Pearson correlation
n = len(american)
mean_a = statistics.mean(american)
mean_g = statistics.mean(grand_total)

numerator = sum((a - mean_a) * (g - mean_g) for a, g in zip(american, grand_total))
denom_a = sum((a - mean_a)**2 for a in american)
denom_g = sum((g - mean_g)**2 for g in grand_total)
pearson_r = numerator / (denom_a * denom_g)**0.5

print(f'Mean American: {mean_a:.4f}')
print(f'Mean Grand Total: {mean_g:.4f}')
print(f'Pearson r: {pearson_r:.6f}')
print(f'Pearson r (3 decimals): {round(pearson_r, 3):.3f}')

# Percentage for Jan, Feb, Mar 1941
jan_am = 468
feb_am = 489
mar_am = 553
total_am = jan_am + feb_am + mar_am

jan_gt = 1825
feb_gt = 1801
mar_gt = 2032
total_gt = jan_gt + feb_gt + mar_gt

pct = (total_am / total_gt) * 100
print(f'American vessels Jan+Feb+Mar: {total_am}')
print(f'Grand total Jan+Feb+Mar: {total_gt}')
print(f'Percentage: {pct:.4f}%')
print(f'Percentage (1 decimal): {round(pct, 1):.1f}')

print()
print(f'ANSWER: [{round(pct, 1):.1f}, {round(pearson_r, 3):.3f}]')
"

mean_g = statistics.mean(grand_total)
